messages:
maria-ml: Heads up — our eval harness is showing nondeterministic outputs for redwood-v2-quant4 on the webqa eval. Same seed (42), same prompt, different tokens across repeated runs.

sasha-research: repro steps?

maria-ml: run: ```python run_eval.py --model redwood-v2-quant4 --seed 42 --top_p 0.92 --temp 0.8 --batch-size 8 --ckpt quantized/4bit``` two runs back-to-back produce different answers in ~15% of prompts.

oliver-ci: CI job 1234 flaked too: https://ci.internal/1234 — logs show different token streams between retries.

kevin-eng: quick datapoint: when we set `temp=0.0` (greedy) outputs are identical across runs, so RNG is definitely involved.

raj-sre: could be worker reuse / RNG pool. Do we reseed / restore per-request RNG state? continuous batching might interleave draws.

maria-ml: interestingly, when I disable continuous batching the nondet disappears. Enabled continuous batching + quant kernels -> divergence.

sasha-research: can you paste a minimal trace / log showing the divergence? any kernel info?

maria-ml: snippet:
```
[eval] req id=abcd seed=42 top_p=0.92 temp=0.8
tokens: "The capital of France is "
generated runA: "Paris."
generated runB: "paris."
logprob diff at token 5: -0.23 vs -0.27
kernel: q4_gemm_v2 / fused_attn_kernel
worker_id: gpu-3 worker_epoch=5
rng_state: saved
```

kevin-eng: lowercase vs uppercase suggests sampling path diverged early. small float diffs from quant rounding can shift the top_p cutoff which flips the candidate set, so a single RNG draw difference gives totally different continuation.

raj-sre: action items: instrument RNG draw counts and tag per-request RNG stream id. Also check snapshot/warmstart behavior for RNG offsets on workers.

oliver-ci: I added a CI smoke that runs the same prompt 10x with `--seed=42` on the quant harness. job 1235 queued.

ci-bot: job 1235 finished: 2/10 mismatches.

sasha-research: proposed plan: 1) deterministic test (`seeded + temp=0.0`) must be stable, 2) sampling stability test (repeat seeded runs with common sampling params), 3) run comparators across kernel variants (q4 vs fp16).

maria-ml: more notes: this only reproduces when (a) quant kernels are used and (b) continuous batching reorders batch members. Suggests RNG advancement depends on batch ordering.

kevin-eng: dug into the worker RNG: it's a per-worker Philox stream advanced per-token by op_count. When we assemble batches we compute per-request offsets but there's a race: batch member reorder + reuse doesn't update offsets deterministically. Fix candidate: store and restore explicit per-request RNG offset at request boundaries, and assert offsets monotonic in tests.

raj-sre: also confirm that when we checkpoint worker state (for warmstart/eviction) we persist RNG offset. Otherwise resumed workers pick up stale offsets.

maria-ml: I'll prototype a repro toggling `shuffle_batches=true/false` and measure mismatch rate. early numbers: shuffle_on = true => ~12% mismatch, shuffle_off => 0.2%.

oliver-ci: suggestion: CI gating: fail on mismatches for `temp=0` tests (should be 0%), and for seeded sampling tests require a very low tolerance post-fix. currently too flaky to block merges.

sasha-research: I'll add a short onboarding section for new models: "run quant vs fp16 sanity + seeded stability sweep (5 seeds)" and log kernel variant and batch config.

maria-ml: tl;dr: root cause likely batch-reorder + per-worker RNG offset bug combined with quant rounding sensitivity at the top_p cutoff. Next steps: kevin to implement per-request RNG restore, raj to validate checkpointing of offsets, sasha + I add CI tests and a small reproducible harness. I'll open a PR and link here. :eyes:

maria-ml: PR opened: https://git.internal/p/redwood/repo/pulls/789 — adds per-request RNG restore & unit tests for batch reordering. tagging @kevin-eng @raj-sre @sasha-research

kevin-eng: ack, starting implementation. will ping when I have a draft.
